<a id="implementation-checkpoints"></a>

## 2. Implementation Checkpoints

| Checkpoint                            | Recorded result and limits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Source/history                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Native foundation and Text/Button     | Approved typed theme/package/showcase boundary; outside-workspace archive/React/provider and local two-platform checks pass. Clipping/label and three P2 remediations are retained; owner visual/physical and inherited palette concerns remain separate. | 65a1b16, be3e4c7; former native ledger sections 8.1–8.16                                                            |
| Basic controls and Select/ListBoxItem | Source, consumer and focused installed guards/ownership/layout proof recorded; maintained Input viewport correction preserves unpaced entry and owner state.                                                                                              | Former ledger 8.17–8.20; PR #17 history retained in Git                                                             |
| TextArea/Radio/RadioGroup             | Source and maintained scene in 1807084, abb2a0b, 9aa5372; focused host fixes 7f8bd96/0aba8c5; 200 source cases at that checkpoint, not today's whole-catalogue acceptance.                                                                                | Former ledger 8.21–8.22                                                                                             |
| NumberInput                           | Bounded raw draft/committed model; explicit consumer Intl preparation; source, frozen-consumer and normal/large Android/iOS proof. Palette, ARM/physical/signing remain separate.                                                                         | Former ledger 8.23–8.25; native controls integrated through PR #18                                                  |
| Modal/AlertDialog                     | Controlled provider/leaf host ownership and maintained chain source exist; focused Select chain later passes while broader overlay/long-content acceptance remains open.                                                                                  | 13f267c source/consumer checkpoint; former ledger 8.27–8.32                                                         |

## 3. Catalogue Acceptance Matrix

This is the active M2 completion ledger for all 53 stable catalogue IDs. Gate definitions, exact scenario IDs and required platform profiles live in [the acceptance rubric](roadmap.md#31-acceptance-rubric). A cell ID is `CAT.<manifest-id>.G<n>`; native scenario cells extend it with platform/profile/scenario/case as specified there. Every mandatory capability and scenario must be instantiated and resolved before its aggregate gate can pass. An empty or uninstantiated scenario set is not vacuous success.

Historical passes retain their recorded scope and artifacts; opening a broader aggregate cell does not invalidate those receipts or promote them to full current-matrix acceptance. The positive restoration checks expose a shared activation defect: NativeOverlayProvider's window predicate reads the live registry, but the application floating host does not rerender on a native dismissal alone. Its scope can remain disabled after the window returns. Subscribe the provider to its owned registry with the existing useSyncExternalStore pattern; no API, native schema, dependency or palette change is needed. Two public Modal/AlertDialog regressions assert application scope enablement before admission, disablement through presentation/closing and re-enablement after the actual iOS dismissal callback, without another owner render. Explicit initialFocusRef/restoreFocusRef accept View/TextInput refs and reject DOM/focus-shaped objects in compiled private contracts. Entry waits for shown/active presentation, measured layout, native scope acknowledgement and foreground state. A request does not change the observed-focus registry; only the original native focus event acknowledges completion. Explicit null or ineligible targets do not select a fallback. Current scoped Escape respects keyboard guards, original down/up/repeat/cancel/default-capture metadata and the deepest floating layer's exit barrier, preserving repeated onOpenChange(false) requests while an owner holds true.

Return capture precedes overlay admission and retains a real native target/binding/window lease. Actual iOS dismissal and Android hidden-frame barriers precede parent restoration, which waits for the parent's fresh native policy acknowledgement. Removed or replaced target/ref, new native epoch, background/active in one batch, reopened owner and unmount retire old work. No queued callback survives teardown. Synchronous teardown return is admitted only if the surviving parent/target is already valid and ready; full ancestor/teardown restoration remains OPEN where readiness has not returned. Automatic first-descendant traversal, forward/backward containment, physical keyboard/speech and actual native acknowledgements remain mandatory separate capabilities.

The failed observation interleaves the first change, an owner commit and result replacement before the remaining key-callback batch. This identifies an ordering difference worth isolating; it does not prove the render or async replacement lost characters, nor reconstruct UIKit application timing.

The exact installed RN 0.86.3 source was inspected and copied with SHA-256 identities into the private packet:

- Fabric RCTTextInputComponentView.mm emits onKeyPress inside textInputShouldChangeText before acceptance/change publication. Default maxLength is int max and the fixture sets no limit. Key callbacks therefore establish proposals at that boundary, not accepted/applied edits.
- RCTBackedTextInputDelegateAdapter.mm calls the proposal delegate, then sets textDidChangeIsComing when it accepts the same replacement. EditingChanged clears that flag and calls textInputDidChange. Its pending-change fallback on end editing is a possible branch, not observed execution in the original failure.
- Fabric textInputDidChange has JS-origin and next-change suppression branches; updateState/setTextAndSelection guard controlled feedback with event-count equality. Neither the original JS trace nor the later post-verdict capture can identify every branch taken during typing.
- TextInput.js rebuilds setLocalRef when mostRecentEventCount changes. useMergeRefs/useRefEffect can clean up and reassign the same instance when that callback changes. This supplies an upstream explanation for the recorded same-instance ref callbacks; those callbacks do not establish a native view remount. No Codon ref/synchronization patch is justified by their presence.

A private observer variant changes only the post-focused-verdict hold so both raw conditions can receive read-only UIKit/KVC snapshots. Its binary SHA-256 is 033de169c329e6697c1f070ea1ee9c9aa4bb233c687d8b2dd6da31e72d620de1. The Release application remains byte-identical; the observer is a distinct condition from prior inspector4a645f3d. The variant builds, and its snapshot expression passes a syntax check against the installed simulator SDK. Six result-parser cases preserve failed focused verdicts and exclude later debugger time, four native-session-progress cases pass, and six host-binding cases fail closed on wrong/reused process identities: **16 focused private cases pass**. These are helper/source checks, not new native input proof.
